A stronger taste preference does not remove the need for appropriate adjustment.

segments.source: Begin with one new bag. Retain the packaging, note the roast and opening dates and make the drink you use most. Keep the first comparison simple enough that another household member can repeat it. A tasting notebook is useful when it records your recipe and preference; it need not pretend to be a laboratory protocol.

segments.source: After two or three controlled drinks, decide which question remains. If the coffee seems too concentrated, investigate ratio. If the flow is very different, investigate grind and preparation. If the roast direction is simply wrong for your preference, compare a different direction rather than making increasingly extreme adjustments to defend the purchase.

If one bag must satisfy several drinkers, include their normal drinks in the decision before subscribing.
